content.user_title: Master Prompt and Context Engineering for AI Agents
content.value_statement: Vague, bloated prompts waste context and produce unreliable AI agent behavior. This skill applies Anthropic context-engineering principles to help you write clear, structured, high-signal prompts that improve accuracy and reduce token cost.
actual_capabilities: Explains context engineering principles: finite attention budget, signal-to-noise optimization, and progressive information discovery.
Provides Markdown structure standards with distinct Background, Instructions, Examples, and Constraints sections.
Supplies reusable templates for context files, agent definitions, and command definitions.
Includes a create-prompt workflow that guides building a new prompt from goal to tested result.
Includes an optimize-prompt workflow that reduces verbosity, removes redundancy, and adds structure to existing prompts.
Offers a best-practices checklist and a list of anti-patterns to review prompts against.
limitations: Provides written guidance and templates only; it does not run code, call tools, or automatically rewrite prompts.
Focuses on prompt and context structure, not on model-specific tuning, evaluation harnesses, or fine-tuning.
Does not measure token counts or performance for you; testing and iteration remain manual.
Principles are general and may need adaptation for a specific model, domain, or product.

use_cases.title: Design a new system prompt
use_cases.description: A developer building an AI agent uses the create-prompt workflow and template sections to write a clear, well-structured system prompt from the start.

use_cases.title: Trim a bloated prompt
use_cases.description: An engineer applies the optimize-prompt workflow to cut redundant text, convert suggestions into direct instructions, and reduce context cost while keeping quality.

use_cases.title: Standardize team prompt quality
use_cases.description: A team lead adopts the best-practices checklist and anti-pattern list as a review standard so all agent prompts across the team follow the same conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Get started with prompt structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the prompting skill, help me structure a prompt for an assistant that summarizes support tickets. Organize it into Background, Instructions, Examples, and Constraints sections.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an existing prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the optimize-prompt workflow to this prompt. Remove redundancy, make instructions direct, and add clear structure. Show the before and after.

prompt_templates.title: Apply progressive information discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt and rewrite it to use just-in-time context loading. Replace inline data dumps with lightweight references that load detail only when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a prompt against the checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this agent prompt against the prompting skill best-practices checklist and anti-patterns. List each item that passes or fails and give a concrete fix for every failure.

output_examples.input: Help me structure a prompt for a code review assistant.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a prompt organized into four sections: Background (the assistant reviews pull requests for correctness and style), Instructions (imperative steps such as read the diff, flag defects, suggest fixes), Examples (a sample finding), and Constraints (report format, severity levels, and scope limits).

output_examples.input: Optimize a verbose 300-word prompt full of hedging language.
output_examples.output: The skill rewrites the prompt into a shorter version: suggestions become direct instructions, repeated points are merged, paragraphs become bulleted lists, and long inline examples are replaced with references. The result covers the same requirements in far fewer tokens.

best_practices: Structure every prompt with clear Markdown sections so each part has one purpose.
Write instructions in direct imperative voice and remove hedging words like might, could, and should consider.
Load detailed data just in time through references instead of dumping full context up front.
anti_patterns: Filling the prompt with verbose explanations and historical background that add tokens without adding signal.
Repeating the same instruction or overlapping tool definitions across multiple places.
Loading large data sets or full schemas into the prompt before they are actually needed.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides standards, templates, and workflows for writing and improving prompts for AI agents, based on Anthropic context-engineering principles.

faq.question: Does the skill run any code or commands?
faq.answer: No. It contains only Markdown documentation and templates. It does not execute scripts, access the network, or modify files.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and its principles apply to prompting for large language models in general.

faq.question: Is this for beginners or experts?
faq.answer: Both. Beginners get clear structure templates and a checklist, while experienced engineers get context-cost reduction and progressive-discovery techniques.

faq.question: What is context engineering?
faq.answer: It is the practice of curating the smallest set of high-signal tokens during inference so the model has exactly what it needs and nothing that wastes its attention budget.

faq.question: Will it automatically rewrite my prompts?
faq.answer: It guides the rewrite through workflows and checklists, but you review and apply the changes. Testing and iteration remain in your control.
